# Control Narrative: Kiln Baghouse BH-700 (DRAFT)

> **Status:** Draft, based on operator input from Dave (shift supervisor). Items marked **[TBC]** are assumptions or values that need confirmation before programming. Open questions are collected in Section 8. **Do not issue for programming until Section 8 is resolved.** Section 6 covers fire and trip functions, which need engineering and safety review.

---

## 1. Purpose

This section defines the start-up, normal operation, shutdown, and protective functions for baghouse BH-700. BH-700 serves the kiln exhaust.

## 2. Equipment

| Tag | Description | Control / Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| SC-701 | Dust discharge screw conveyor | Start/stop, run feedback [TBC: zero-speed switch?] |
| RV-702 | Rotary airlock | Start/stop, run feedback [TBC: zero-speed switch?] |
| F-703 | ID fan | Start/stop [TBC: VFD speed ref?], run/at-speed feedback |
| D-704 | Baghouse inlet damper | Open/close [TBC: or modulating], position feedback |
| D-706 | Bleed-air (dilution) damper | Open/close [TBC: or modulating], position feedback |
| TT-705 | Baghouse inlet temperature | Analog, °F |
| PDT-7xx | Baghouse differential pressure | Analog, in. w.c. **[TBC: tag number not provided]** |
| — | Pulse-jet cleaning solenoids | One output per row [TBC: number of rows] |
| — | Kiln feed | Interlock output to kiln feed system [TBC: interface] |

## 3. Modes

- **Auto:** The sequences in Sections 4 and 5 run from a single Start or Stop command.
- **Manual:** Each device runs individually from HMI. Interlocks in Section 6 remain active in all modes [TBC: confirm which interlocks, if any, may be bypassed, and under what authorization].

## 4. Start-Up Sequence (Auto)

The order is downstream first: discharge equipment is proven running before the fan pulls dust into the hopper.

| Step | Action | Proceed When | Fault If |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm D-704 closed and all start permissives healthy | Permissives OK | Not OK: start inhibited, alarm |
| 2 | Start SC-701 | SC-701 run feedback confirmed | No feedback in [10 s TBC]: abort, alarm |
| 3 | Start RV-702 | RV-702 run feedback confirmed | No feedback in [10 s TBC]: abort, alarm |
| 4 | Start F-703 | F-703 at speed / run confirmed | No feedback in [30 s TBC]: abort, alarm |
| 5 | Start fan-stabilization timer, operator-adjustable, default **60 s** | Timer complete | — |
| 6 | Open D-704 | D-704 open confirmed | Not open in [30 s TBC]: alarm |
| 7 | Enable pulse cleaning (Section 5.1). Baghouse is now **Running** | — | — |

**Note on sequence:** The operators currently differ. Dave starts SC-701 and RV-702 first. Mike starts F-703 first. This narrative uses Dave's order. The fan cannot pull gas through the bags until D-704 opens, so starting the fan first gives no anti-blinding benefit. **[TBC: confirm with operations.]**

## 5. Normal Operation

### 5.1 Pulse Cleaning

- Cleaning is time-based and sequential. One row is pulsed per interval, cycling through all rows continuously.
- **Normal interval:** 10 s between rows (operator-adjustable).
- **High-DP interval:** 5 s between rows (operator-adjustable).
- **Switch to high-DP interval** when DP ≥ **6.0 in. w.c.** for [10 s TBC].
- **Return to normal interval** when DP ≤ **[5.0 in. w.c. TBC]** for [60 s TBC]. This deadband prevents rapid toggling.
- **Pulse (valve-open) duration:** [TBC, typically 100–200 ms per bag supplier].
- Cleaning runs whenever F-703 is running, including during the shutdown clean-down (Section 5.4).

### 5.2 Differential Pressure Alarms

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| DP High | ≥ 6.0 in. w.c. | Alarm; switch to high-DP interval (5.1) |
| DP High-High | ≥ 8.0 in. w.c. for [30 s TBC] | Alarm; **stop kiln feed** [TBC: automatic interlock or operator action; see 8.4] |

### 5.3 Inlet Temperature Protection

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| TT-705 High | ≥ 450 °F | Alarm; open D-706 |
| TT-705 Reset | ≤ [425 °F TBC] for [60 s TBC] | Close D-706 |
| TT-705 High-High | [TBC] | [TBC: e.g., stop kiln feed / close D-704] |

The 450 °F limit must be checked against the bag media rating on the bag datasheet.

### 5.4 Shutdown Sequence (Auto, Normal Stop)

| Step | Action | Proceed When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [TBC: confirm kiln feed is stopped / kiln is off-line as a stop permissive] | Confirmed |
| 2 | Close D-704 [TBC: or leave open during clean-down; see 8.6] | D-704 closed confirmed |
| 3 | F-703 keeps running. Pulse cleaning continues at normal interval. Start clean-down timer, default **10 min** (adjustable) | Timer complete |
| 4 | Stop pulse cleaning; stop F-703 | F-703 stopped confirmed |
| 5 | SC-701 and RV-702 keep running for [5 min TBC] to empty the hopper | Timer complete |
| 6 | Stop RV-702, then SC-701 | Stopped. Baghouse is **Stopped** |

## 6. Interlocks and Trips

> **Safety note:** Dave reports a hopper fire in 2019 linked to airlock failure. The functions below protect against fire and equipment damage. They should be reviewed in a hazard study (PHA/HAZOP), and the team should decide whether any must be implemented as safety instrumented functions rather than BPCS logic. The trip actions below are **proposed** and must be confirmed.

| # | Initiator | Proposed Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| I-1 | RV-702 failure (loss of run feedback / zero-speed) while Running | Alarm; stop kiln feed; close D-704; [TBC: stop or keep F-703] | Dave: "shut everything down quick." See 8.3 on whether stopping the fan is safe for the kiln |
| I-2 | SC-701 failure while RV-702 running | Stop RV-702, then apply I-1 actions | Not stated by Dave. Standard downstream interlock [TBC] |
| I-3 | F-703 failure while Running | Alarm; close D-704; [TBC: stop kiln feed] | Not stated by Dave [TBC] |
| I-4 | DP High-High | See 5.2 | |
| I-5 | TT-705 High / High-High | See 5.3 | |
| I-6 | Start permissives | Start inhibited unless SC-701 and RV-702 are proven running before F-703, and F-703 is proven running before D-704 opens | Enforced in Auto and [TBC] Manual |

## 7. Operator-Adjustable Parameters

These parameters can be changed from HMI, within engineering limits [TBC]:

- Fan-stabilization timer (60 s)
- Normal and high-DP pulse intervals (10 s / 5 s)
- DP High setpoint and reset (6.0 / 5.0 in.)
- Clean-down timer (10 min)
- TT-705 reset setpoint

The DP High-High setpoint, the TT-705 High/High-High setpoints, and the trip delays should be **engineering-access only** [TBC].

## 8. Open Items (Resolve Before Programming)

1. **Start order:** Confirm conveyor/airlock first (Dave) versus fan first (Mike). The draft uses Dave's order.
2. **DP transmitter:** Provide tag number and range.
3. **Airlock trip scope (I-1):** Define "shut everything down." Stopping F-703 while the kiln is firing may cause kiln draft loss or positive pressure. Process engineering must decide whether the fan stops, keeps running, or the kiln trips.
4. **DP > 8 in.:** Dave said they "usually" shut kiln feed. Decide whether this is an automatic interlock or an alarm with operator action.
5. **Hopper protection:** Given the 2019 fire, consider adding a hopper high-level switch, zero-speed switches on RV-702 and SC-701, and a hopper or outlet temperature alarm. None of these are in the current description.
6. **Clean-down with D-704:** Decide whether the inlet damper should be closed or open during the 10-minute clean-down. Confirm the kiln is offline first.
7. **TT-705 response:** Decide whether D-706 is on/off or modulating. Provide reset setpoint, High-High action, and bag media temperature rating.
8. **Pulse system details:** Number of rows, pulse duration, and compressed-air pressure permissive (low air pressure alarm).
9. **Low DP alarm:** Not mentioned. A low DP often indicates broken bags. Decide whether to add one.
10. **Restart after trip:** Decide whether a trip requires manual reset at HMI before restart.
11. **Kiln interface:** Define signals to and from the kiln control system, such as kiln feed stop and kiln running status.

---

I'd recommend reviewing Section 8 with Dave, Mike, and process engineering together. Items 3 and 5 relate directly to the 2019 fire and shouldn't be left to the integrator's judgment.
